answer.rationale:
Rollback is ruled out by compliance, so memory_b1 (the strongest inherited success pattern) is unavailable regardless of how good it looks. That leaves failover vs. offload as the live options, and the two I want verified are exactly the two whose original records could change the decision.

Why verify memory_b2: it is the closest match to the surface facts (latency degradation confined to one region, failover fixed it fast). But the consolidated summary says 'traffic shifted cleanly' without saying whether the March event was write-heavy or whether replication was synchronous. Our primary objective explicitly forbids losing customer writes, and we are at peak settlement write volume. If the March degradation was read-path or low-write, that memory does not license a failover now, and the confident phrasing 'recovered within minutes' would be exactly the kind of compressed success story that hides the precondition that mattered.

Why verify memory_b5: it is my current intent, and it depends on an unstated causal claim — that write latency on the primary was being driven by read contention. If the original record shows the primary was contended by report/dashboard reads (as the summary implies), then offloading reads is the one intervention that can relieve the primary without moving or risking in-flight writes. If instead the write latency there had an independent cause, this action is cosmetic and I have burned the single window.

Current intent is read-replica routing at small guarded scale: it is reversible, it does not relocate the write path during peak settlement, and it fails safe — if it does not help, we lose latency headroom but not writes, whereas a failover that mishandles in-flight writes violates the primary objective outright. I am deliberately starting narrow rather than broad because the causal story is unverified.

Uncertainty and downstream risk I am not resolving: (1) I do not know the real driver of the 90-minute climb; it may be the new release's write path even though the build cannot be reverted, in which case a circuit breaker or capacity add is the better next-window move. (2) Routing reads to replicas introduces replica lag on settlement-adjacent reads — any downstream reconciliation, fraud scoring, or balance display consuming those reads may act on stale state, which is a correctness risk propagating past this incident, not just a latency tradeoff. (3) All six inherited memories are success stories with no recorded failures or non-actions, so the archive is survivorship-biased; I am treating their confidence as weaker than their phrasing. I will record the actual outcome, including the causal ambiguity, rather than consolidating another clean win.
